subject: Physics
source_note: Compiled from the NTA JEE Main 2026 Information Bulletin / official syllabus (Section A: Units 1-19 theory, Section B: Unit 20 Experimental Skills) as reported by multiple 2025-2026 coaching/exam-tracker sources, cross-checked Sep 2026. Communication Systems was removed from the syllabus in the 2024-25 rationalisation and no longer appears as a unit. Always verify against the current-year NTA information bulletin (jeemain.nta.nic.in) before finalising a question bank, since NTA can revise the syllabus PDF between sessions.
exam_pattern_note: JEE Main Paper 1 Physics: 25 questions total (Section A: 20 single-correct MCQs, Section B: 5 numerical-value questions, all 25 compulsory since the 2025 pattern change removed the earlier 'attempt any 5 of 10' choice in Section B). No multiple-correct or matrix-match question types appear in JEE Main (those are JEE-Advanced-only formats).

subtopics: SI units, fundamental and derived units, dimensional formulae
Dimensional analysis and its applications (checking equations, deriving relations)
Errors in measurement: absolute, relative, percentage error; error propagation in sums, differences, products, quotients
Significant figures and rounding rules
topics.syllabus_change_note: 2025 rationalisation dropped 'physics, technology and society' and a standalone line on accuracy/precision of instruments as separately examinable; core dimensional-analysis and error-propagation content is unchanged.

subtopics: Motion in a straight line: position-time and velocity-time graphs
Motion in a plane, projectile motion
Uniform circular motion
Relative velocity in one and two dimensions
Newton's three laws of motion and their applications
Law of conservation of linear momentum and its applications
Equilibrium of concurrent forces
Static and kinetic friction, laws of friction, rolling friction (qualitative)
Dynamics of uniform circular motion: centripetal force, banking of roads
Work done by a constant and a variable force
Work-energy theorem, kinetic and potential energy
Conservative forces, conservation of mechanical energy
Elastic and inelastic collisions in one and two dimensions
Power, definitions and units
Centre of mass of a system of particles, motion of the centre of mass
Moment of inertia, radius of gyration
Parallel and perpendicular axes theorems (for simple, symmetric bodies only)
Moment of inertia of a uniform ring, disc, thin rod, sphere and cylinder (standard results)
Angular momentum, torque, conservation of angular momentum
Equilibrium of rigid bodies, rolling motion
Universal law of gravitation
Acceleration due to gravity and its variation with altitude and depth
Kepler's laws of planetary motion
Gravitational potential energy, gravitational potential, escape velocity
Orbital velocity of a satellite
topics.syllabus_change_note: 2025 rationalisation dropped the standalone 'geostationary satellites' bullet; general orbital-velocity and satellite-motion content remains examinable.

subtopics: Elastic behaviour of materials, stress-strain relationship, Hooke's law
Young's modulus, bulk modulus, modulus of rigidity
Pressure in a fluid, Pascal's law, buoyancy
Surface energy and surface tension, angle of contact, drops, bubbles, capillary rise
Viscosity, Stokes' law, terminal velocity
Streamline flow, equation of continuity, Bernoulli's theorem and its applications
topics.syllabus_change_note: 2025 rationalisation dropped 'Reynolds number' and 'Newton's law of cooling' from this unit as separately examinable line items.

subtopics: Thermal equilibrium and the zeroth law of thermodynamics
Heat, work and internal energy, first law of thermodynamics
Specific heat capacity, Cv and Cp for an ideal gas
Isothermal and adiabatic processes
Second law of thermodynamics, reversible and irreversible processes
topics.syllabus_change_note: 2025 rationalisation dropped 'Carnot engine and its efficiency' as a directly examinable derivation-heavy sub-item; the qualitative second-law content remains.

subtopics: Equation of state of a perfect gas, work done in compressing a gas
Kinetic theory assumptions, concept of pressure
Kinetic interpretation of temperature, rms speed of gas molecules
Degrees of freedom, law of equipartition of energy, applications to specific heats
Mean free path, Avogadro's number
Periodic motion, simple harmonic motion (SHM) and its equation
Simple pendulum, spring-mass system, energy in SHM
Wave motion: longitudinal and transverse waves, speed of a travelling wave
Superposition of waves, progressive and standing waves
Vibration of strings and air columns, resonance tube, beats
topics.syllabus_change_note: 2025 rationalisation dropped standalone treatment of forced/damped oscillations, mechanical resonance as a separate derivation, and the Doppler effect in sound; basic SHM, standing waves and beats remain.

subtopics: Coulomb's law, electric field, field lines, electric dipole and dipole field
Torque on a dipole in a uniform electric field
Electric flux, Gauss's law and its applications (infinite line/sheet, spherical shell)
Electric potential, potential due to a point charge and a dipole, equipotential surfaces
Capacitance, parallel-plate capacitor with and without a dielectric
Capacitors in series and parallel, energy stored in a capacitor
Electric current, drift velocity, Ohm's law
Resistance, resistivity and their temperature dependence
Series and parallel combinations of resistors and of cells
Kirchhoff's laws and simple applications (Wheatstone bridge, meter bridge)
Potentiometer: principle and applications
Heating effects of current, electrical power

topics.chapter: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
subtopics: Biot-Savart law and Ampere's law, applications to a straight wire, loop and solenoid
Force on a moving charge and on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
Torque on a current loop, moving coil galvanometer and its conversion to an ammeter/voltmeter
Magnetic dipole moment of a current loop
Bar magnet as an equivalent solenoid, qualitative magnetic properties of materials
Faraday's laws of electromagnetic induction, Lenz's law
Self-inductance and mutual inductance
Alternating currents, peak and rms values
AC circuit with a series LCR combination, resonance, power factor
AC generator and transformer (principle and working)
Displacement current (qualitative)
Electromagnetic waves and their characteristics (qualitative), transverse nature
Electromagnetic spectrum and typical uses of its bands (radio to gamma rays)
Reflection and refraction at plane and spherical surfaces, mirror and lens formulae, total internal reflection
Thin lens formula, lens maker's formula, power of a lens, combination of thin lenses
Refraction through a prism, dispersion
Optical instruments: simple/compound microscope, telescope (magnifying power)
Wave nature of light, Huygens' principle
Young's double-slit interference, single-slit diffraction
Polarisation: plane polarised light, Brewster's law, Polaroids
topics.syllabus_change_note: JEE Main keeps Ray Optics and Wave Optics as one combined unit, unlike the split used in some other exams.

topics.chapter: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
subtopics: Photoelectric effect, Einstein's photoelectric equation
Particle nature of light: the photon
Matter waves, de Broglie relation
Alpha-particle scattering, Rutherford's model, Bohr model of the atom, energy levels and the hydrogen spectrum
Composition and size of the nucleus, mass-energy relation, mass defect
Binding energy per nucleon and its variation with mass number
Radioactivity: alpha, beta and gamma decay
Nuclear fission and fusion
topics.syllabus_change_note: 2025 rationalisation trimmed the explicit alpha/beta/gamma decay-equation derivations; qualitative radioactivity and the decay-law numerical remain examinable.

subtopics: Semiconductors, energy bands in solids (qualitative: conductors, insulators, semiconductors)
p-n junction diode, I-V characteristics in forward and reverse bias
Diode as a rectifier
LED, photodiode, solar cell, and Zener diode as a voltage regulator
Logic gates (OR, AND, NOT, NAND, NOR) and their truth tables
topics.syllabus_change_note: Not part of the JEE Advanced syllabus at all — this is a JEE-Main-only unit. 2025 rationalisation dropped transistor amplifier/oscillator circuit analysis, keeping only qualitative diode/logic-gate behaviour.

subtopics: Vernier callipers and screw gauge: least count, use in measuring length/diameter
Determination of g using a simple pendulum
Young's modulus by Searle's method
Surface tension by capillary rise method
Coefficient of viscosity by measuring terminal velocity of a sphere
Specific heat of a solid/liquid by the method of mixtures
Speed of sound in air using a resonance column
Verification of Ohm's law using a voltmeter and ammeter
Resistance and resistivity using a metre bridge / post office box
Focal length of a concave mirror and a convex lens using the u-v method
Characteristic curves of a p-n junction diode and of a Zener diode
Using a multimeter to measure resistance, voltage, current and to check the continuity/polarity of a diode
topics.syllabus_change_note: This is a dedicated 20th syllabus unit in JEE Main (Section B of the syllabus, distinct from Section B of the exam paper which is the numerical-value question block). JEE Advanced folds most of the same experiments into its 'Units, Dimensions, Errors and Experimental Physics' topic rather than listing them as a separate unit.
